Hi! I don’t know if this is the correct place to post this, so feel free to delete if it’s not.

I have a list of URLs as follows:

```
2025-11-22: (Color Palette Pro — A Synthesizer for Color Palettes)[https://colorpalette.pro]  
2025-11-22: (A Trail Tale)[https://atrailtale.com/#/]  
2025-11-22: (Stickertop)[https://stickertop.art/main/]  
```

They are formatted incorrectly in Markdown, and I want to record a macro that would correct them — that is, change parentheses to square brackets and vice versa. For example, `2025-11-22: (A Trail Tale)[https://atrailtale.com/#/]` should become `2025-11-22: [A Trail Tale](https://atrailtale.com/#/)`.

In Neovim with the MiniMax configuration (with the most recent commits), I recorded the following macro:
`0f(%r]<80><fd>5``r[<80><fd>5f[%r)<80><fd>5``r(`
(By the way, does anybody know why <80><fd>5 is recorded and what keypress it represents?)

However, when I replay the macro, I get an unexpected result:

```
# Macro replayed from the second URL
2025-11-22: [Color Palette Pro — A Synthesizer for Color Palettes](https://colorpalette.pro)  
2025-11-22: [A Trail Tale][https://atrailtale.com/#/]  
(025-11-22: )Stickertop)[https://stickertop.art/main/]
```

When I record the same macro in Neovim started with the `--clean` argument, the following command is recorded:
`0f(<80><fd>5%r]<80><fd>5``r[<80><fd>5f[<80><fd>5%r)<80><fd>5``r(`
There are additional `<80><fd>5` sequences added, but I don’t think they affect anything. When this macro is replayed in Neovim with the default configuration, everything works as expected.

Can anyone recommend how to troubleshoot this situation or has any idea what might be causing the problem? A potential hint is that in one of my previous attempts, the macro replaced parentheses with square brackets, but then threw `E756: spellcheck is not possible` and did not change the square brackets to parentheses.

comment_data.body:
Not sure about the problem with this particular macro, but here is the macro I'd do it with: `0srn)]srn])j` . What it does:
- `0` - move to line start.
- `srn)]` - replace next `)` surrounding with `]` surrounding.
- `srn])` - replace next `]` surrounding with `)` surrounding.
- `j` - go to the next line (helps with "chaining" macro).

reply_data.body:
> (By the way, does anybody know why <80>5 is recorded and what keypress it represents?)

The `<80><fd>5` is a keycode for `<Ignore>` special word. It is probably used in `%` mapping that comes from 'matchit.vim' (plugin bundled and enabled by Neovim itself, not MiniMax).

Is ``` 0f(%r]``r[f[%r)``r( ``` a sequence of keys that you pressed? I indeed can reproduce this. After some debugging, it looks like an issue with *combination* of 'mini.clue' and 'mini.jump'. Disabling either one makes it work as expected.

Although enabled 'mini.clue' [might lead to problems with macros](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/6e885e4c27743ae6bf5957ea78ce86c032835f09/doc/mini-clue.txt#L87-L91), I don't remember I encountered this issue. I'll take a closer look.

Anyway, this is not a MiniMax issue and there is a workaround that uses 'mini.surround' (which I'd recommend using in this case anyway).
